source.title: Over-parameterization as a Catalyst for Better Generalization of Deep ReLU network

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper and supplementary material. Its title differs from the provided ID title: the text is titled “Student Specialization in Deep Rectified Networks With Finite Width and Input Dimension.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies student-node specialization to a fixed teacher network, not convergence between independently trained models as scale or capability increases, nor any of the other specified claim versions. It discusses representation comparisons and CCA but does not test the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theory and experiments on student nodes specializing to a fixed teacher. Those findings are related to representation alignment but do not measure any listed version: the models are in a teacher-student setup, and the experiments do not measure cross-seed model similarity, cross-modal alignment, representation interchangeability, universal features, or metric/data dependence as defined here. The CCA/SVCCA discussion refers to prior work; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains student ReLU networks on a fixed teacher's outputs and measures how well student nodes align with teacher nodes. It never compares independently trained models with each other: no cross-seed, cross-architecture, cross-modal or scale comparison. Its only link to the claim is a discussion of why CCA/SVCCA can align networks from different initializations (Sec. 4), which is theoretical and has no measurement behind it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors prove that, with small per-sample gradients, each teacher node is specialized by at least one over-realized student node at the lowest layer. They give polynomial sample complexity for two-layer networks. Experiments show stronger specialization with more over-realization and samples, and earlier specialization of strong teacher nodes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses teacher-student node alignment and normalized activation correlations, rather than comparing representational distance geometry across independently trained models or scaling model capability.
record.method_sensitivity: Student specialization depends on over-realization, teacher-node strength, sample count, and whether data augmentation is teacher-aware; the paper also reports different behavior across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Over-realized ReLU students specialize to the nodes of a fixed teacher. Specialization strengthens with over-realization and sample count, and is better at the lowest layer. Strong teacher nodes (large fan-out) are matched sooner and more often than weak ones. Unspecialized student nodes have near-zero fan-out weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In teacher-student ReLU training, student nodes recover teacher nodes one-to-many, with recovery depending on over-realization, teacher-node strength, layer depth and data augmentation.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2020, Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning
record.problems: The results address a fixed teacher-student setup rather than the claim's independently trained models. Several empirical correlation outcomes are shown only in figures without exact values or uncertainty estimates. The authors state that their deep-network theory establishes specialization at the lowest layer, with specialization at every layer left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7 and Figure 8 contain additional teacher-node recovery-rate and training-dynamics plots. Their detailed plotted values are not stated in the text; the paper's qualitative findings about teacher strength and specialization are summarized in authors_conclusion and fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Scale or capability trends in alignment across independently trained models.
Students trained from 32 seeds all specialize to the same teacher, but student-to-student similarity across seeds is never measured.
Mapping or stitching between models; CCA alignment is only discussed theoretically.
Recurrence of interpretable features across models.
Dependence of the similarity measure on metric or input choices.
Plateau or causes of cross-model alignment.

missing.what: Teacher-node recovery rate (correlation > 0.95) over 32 seeds, by teacher polarity p and over-realization. Stronger teachers are matched more often. The record declares this as left out.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's title in the text matches arXiv:1909.13458 (ICML 2020). The 'different initializations' link is only in a discussion paragraph claiming Theorems 1–2 explain CCA/SVCCA alignment; no cross-seed comparison is run. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Scale and capability trends in independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
Alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions as model performance changes.
Whether independently initialized networks of the same architecture learn shared features or subspaces; the experiments compare students to a fixed teacher, not students to one another.
Mapping representations between models, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Sensitivity of convergence to similarity metrics, metric settings, or in-/out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.
